editing: Shared iteration 0 together where shown; later methods take turns playing in a fixed row while the other panels freeze. 4×/8× context; selected highlights at 1×.

tasks.title: Stack three blocks
tasks.description: Pick and place two blocks to build a three-block stack.
tasks.story: The first update turns a missed placement into a stable three-block stack. The comparison focuses on the final placement, where the shown baseline evaluations still fail.

chapters.title: The initial policy misses the first placement
chapters.takeaway: All methods start from the same task policy. Here it releases the red block beside the base, leaving the later placement unreached.

chapters.title: After one update, the policy completes both placements
chapters.takeaway: The updated Skill-Space Shooting policy builds a stable stack. In these first-iteration baseline evaluations, HUMAN misses the final placement and DSRL disturbs the stack.

tasks.title: Put away a tape roll
tasks.description: Open the drawer, place the tape roll inside, and close the drawer.
tasks.story: Opening the drawer makes the later grasp, placement, and closing stages reachable. These comparisons show which parts of that sequence the learned policies can execute after further training.

chapters.title: The initial policy cannot open the drawer
chapters.takeaway: The same initial policy is shown in all three panels. Without opening the drawer, the robot cannot reach the placement or closing stages.

chapters.title: One update lets the policy reach the later stages
chapters.takeaway: Skill-Space Shooting gets the tape into the drawer. HUMAN opens the drawer but misses the tape grasp, while DSRL still does not open it in this evaluation.

tasks.title: Prepare an iced drink
tasks.description: Pour milk and coffee into the glass, then add ice and a stirrer.
tasks.story: As the policy reaches later stages, a stirrer-placement failure becomes visible. The last chapter compares our iteration 5 with HUMAN iteration 6 and DSRL iteration 5; each evaluation displays its actual iteration.

tasks.title: Wipe and put away the sponge
tasks.description: Pick up the sponge, wipe the white bowl, and place the sponge in the receiving bowl.
tasks.story: Both conditions run the same improvement loop. Sharing uses 70 new skill demonstrations (10 pick, 50 wipe, 10 place), compared with 150 without sharing (50 per skill). The videos show both task policies improving; sharing reduces the new teaching used to prepare the corrective skills.

chapters.takeaway: With sharing drops the sponge; without sharing leaves it on the white bowl.
